note: Deterministic behavioural specs for the backlog-supervisor prompt. Each deterministic spec names one #118 census clause and supplies the state that exercises it; removing that clause makes the rule unstated and fails the spec. Judgement clauses are explicit deterministic=false exclusions and never enter the score.

specs.description: Workers left by an earlier cycle are collected before new work is launched.
The four-hour stale rule applies to working and collecting workers.
Escalated and split-suggested entries are not reset by the stale rule.
A fresh collecting entry is owned by an overlapping cycle and is skipped.
A collecting entry older than one hour belongs to a dead collector and is reset.
No new worker is launched when the parallel-worker limit is already active.
The cycle token budget stops new launches once collected output exceeds it.
The repository is fetched before the open-issue list is read.
A repository with no open issues is reported as BACKLOG EMPTY and skipped.
The supervisor never creates an issue to fill the backlog.
Auto-filed factory failures wait for human triage and are not dispatched.
An issue with an already-open PR is not picked again.
An issue already assigned to a worker state is not dispatched twice.
The ledger retry guard runs before an issue is picked.
A retry-guarded issue needs a material brief, tier, or skip decision.
A failover action is obeyed before the issue is briefed.
A reflection-carrying failover dispatches with the prior reflection.
The flag_for_operator failover action stops automatic dispatch.
A greenfield issue uses the greenfield brief mode.
An issue whose requested symbol already exists on base is skipped.
An issue whose stated gate has not tripped is skipped.
A stale target worktree is removed before dispatch.
A leftover local or remote worker branch is deleted before dispatch.
The worker worktree is cut from the repository's configured base branch.
Every worker brief has separate SCOPE and ROOM header blocks.
Every worker brief carries a PROOF block or explicitly says none is required.
When a DELIVERABLE line is present, the named path is checked mechanically.
A repair brief consumes parsed structured diagnostics rather than a raw log.
State is never written directly; the atomic state-write path is used.
A collector claims a worker atomically before reviewing it.
Every collected worker gets one outcome row in the metrics ledger.
Is this issue sufficiently well specified to brief?
